cards.explanation: The answer is the mountains of Israel. God says, "Son of man, set your face against the mountains of Israel and prophesy against them." (Ezekiel 6:2) Son of man is what God calls Ezekiel here. So Ezekiel gets his orders: turn and face the mountains, and speak. Not the easiest audience to preach to, friends, but a prophet goes where he's sent.

The answer is their high places. God says, "I am about to bring a sword against you, and I will destroy your high places." (Ezekiel 6:3) He says it again in verse 6: the high places will be demolished. So the high places are right in the middle of this message, friends.

The answer is idols. God says, "…I will cast down your slain before your idols." (Ezekiel 6:4) Verse 5 says it again: He will lay the corpses of the Israelites before their idols. Right in front of the idols. It's a heavy part, friends, so I'll just say it plainly: I think this one hurts.

The answer is False. God says, "Wherever you live, the cities will be laid waste…" (Ezekiel 6:6) So the cities aren't spared. The high places, altars, idols and incense altars are all named in that same verse. It's a long list, friends, and the cities are on it.

The answer is that He is the LORD. God says, "The slain will fall among you, and you will know that I am the LORD." (Ezekiel 6:7) That line comes back again and again in this passage, in verses 10, 13 and 14. God keeps saying it, so it clearly matters, friends. It's the point He keeps coming back to.

The answer is True. God says, "Yet I will leave a remnant, for some of you will escape the sword when you are scattered among the nations and throughout the lands." (Ezekiel 6:8) A remnant is the part that's left. After all that smashing, friends, that one little word opens a door.

The answer is the LORD. God says, "Then in the nations to which they have been carried captive, your survivors will remember Me…" (Ezekiel 6:9) Far from home, they turn their thoughts back to Him. Remembering is where it starts, friends.

The word is loathe. The verse says, "So they will loathe themselves for the evil they have done and for all their abominations." (Ezekiel 6:9) It comes right after they remember how He was grieved by their hearts that turned away. It's a heavy moment, friends, and I think it's a sorrowful one.

The answer is False. God says, "And they will know that I am the LORD; I did not declare in vain that I would bring this calamity upon them." (Ezekiel 6:10) So it was no empty threat. He didn't say it for nothing, friends. His word was real, and they will come to know it.

The answer is to clap his hands and stomp his feet. God says, "Clap your hands, stomp your feet…" (Ezekiel 6:11) He also tells Ezekiel to cry out "Alas!" over the abominations of the house of Israel. So Ezekiel gets a whole-body assignment, friends. No sitting still for this prophet.

The answer is False. God says, "He who is far off will die by the plague, he who is near will fall by the sword, and he who remains will die by famine." (Ezekiel 6:12) Far off, near, or left behind, each one is named. Distance doesn't get anybody out of this picture, friends.

The answer is that they offered fragrant incense to their idols. The verse ends by calling them "…the places where they offered fragrant incense to all their idols." (Ezekiel 6:13) So the hills, mountaintops and leafy oaks were the very spots of their idol worship, friends. That's where the slain will lie.
